name: Orbit AI - Phase 0 - Backup restore test (new, not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Every Sunday at 4am
nodes.notes: 05 Section 12: 'backup restore testing (periodic automated restore-to-scratch, not just a successful log entry).' Weekly, after nightly-backup.workflow.json's 3am slot - a judgment call on cadence (daily would be excessive for a slow-changing check, monthly too infrequent to catch a backup that quietly started failing weeks ago), not brief-specified. Restores into a throwaway scratch database and verifies real data landed, rather than trusting 'the S3 upload succeeded' as proof the backup itself is usable - those are different failure modes (a corrupt/incomplete pg_dump can still upload successfully).

nodes.name: Download latest dump from R2
nodes.notes: Same R2 credential/endpoint caveat as nightly-backup.workflow.json's own upload nodes. ASSUMES this runs the same day a backup was created (both are scheduled - Sunday's restore test checks Sunday's own nightly backup, not an older one) - if a given night's backup ever fails to run, this download will fail too, which is itself a meaningful signal (the two workflows failing together points at nightly-backup, not this one).

nodes.name: Restore into scratch DB

parameters.command: =dropdb -h localhost -U PLACEHOLDER_SCRAPER_DB_USER --if-exists orbit_scratch_restore_test && createdb -h localhost -U PLACEHOLDER_SCRAPER_DB_USER orbit_scratch_restore_test && psql -h localhost -U PLACEHOLDER_SCRAPER_DB_USER -d orbit_scratch_restore_test -f /tmp/orbit-backups/{{ 'scraper-' + $now.format('yyyy-LL-dd') + '.sql' }}

nodes.notes: Drops any leftover scratch DB from a prior failed run before recreating it, so this is safe to re-run without manual cleanup. Restores into a DEDICATED throwaway database (orbit_scratch_restore_test), never the real scraper DB - a restore test that touched production data would be a much worse failure mode than the thing it's testing for.

nodes.name: Verify restored row count

parameters.command: =psql -h localhost -U PLACEHOLDER_SCRAPER_DB_USER -d orbit_scratch_restore_test -t -c "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public') AS table_count;"

nodes.notes: Checks that real tables actually landed (a nonzero table count), not a specific expected row count - this repo doesn't know the scraper DB's real schema from this sandbox, so 'restore produced a populated database' is the honest bar to test for, not 'restore matches an exact expected shape' which would be guessing.

nodes.name: Drop scratch DB
nodes.notes: Always cleans up the scratch DB regardless of what the verify step found, so this workflow never leaves a growing pile of throwaway databases behind - runs unconditionally in the sequence, not gated behind the IF below.

nodes.name: Restore verified?
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: assumes n8n's Execute Command node exposes stdout on `.stdout` for this version - same 'documented assumption, not exercised against a live instance' caveat as every other executeCommand node in this repo (nightly-backup.workflow.json's own).

nodes.name: Alert: restore test passed

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'info', source: 'backup-restore-test', message: 'Weekly backup restore test passed - scratch restore produced ' + $('Verify restored row count').item.json.stdout.trim() + ' tables.' }) }}

nodes.notes: Alerts on SUCCESS too, not just failure - '05 Section 12: periodic automated restore-to-scratch, not just a successful log entry' is specifically about not treating an unverified backup as trustworthy; a positive result here IS the thing worth surfacing, since silence could mean 'passed' or 'never ran' and those need to be distinguishable.

nodes.name: Alert: restore test FAILED

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'critical', source: 'backup-restore-test', message: 'Weekly backup restore test FAILED - the scratch restore produced zero tables. The nightly backup may be unusable. Investigate before trusting it for a real recovery.' }) }}

nodes.notes: Critical severity, not warning - an unusable backup discovered only during a real outage is the whole failure mode this workflow exists to catch early instead.
